FY14.subtitle: From the Birth of Modern Physics to ITER.
FY14.description: An interdisciplinary course taught in English that combines physics, English and French (CLIL). It travels from the birth of modern physics through the energy of the nucleus, fusion in the stars and plasma to the Cold War race for fusion and the international ITER project. The whole course answers one question: if scientists have understood nuclear fusion for almost a century, why is producing electricity from fusion still so difficult?
goals: explain why classical physics was not enough and how quantum physics was born
calculate the energy of nuclear reactions from the mass defect and binding energy
explain why fusion needs extreme temperatures and how magnetic fields confine a plasma
evaluate how politics, cooperation and technology have shaped fusion research
distinguish verified research results from predictions and commercial claims
discuss and write about science in English and get by in everyday situations in French
FY14.overview: The course has about 16 teaching sessions: 8 physics, 5 French and 3 project sessions. The Fotoni lab visit is separate from these sessions. ★ marks optional extra material: it is not required for completing the course.
